title: Positive-energy tube analyticity and discrete-symmetry proof interfaces

items.title: Positive-energy joint spectral input

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019)
references.locator: §5.1, printed p. 24: Definition 24 gives the strongly continuous translation representation, joint PVM, forward-cone support, and its holomorphic extension.

references.title: Jens Mund, General Aspects of Relativistic Quantum Field Theory, incomplete lecture notes, DF-UFJF (2012)
references.locator: §1.3, PDF pp. 8–9, equations (19)–(24): joint momentum spectrum, PVM representation of translations, and the closed forward cone; §2.1, Theorem 2.6, PDF pp. 15–16, for the distinction between reconstructed matrix-coefficient spectrum and joint spectral input.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space
with inner product $(\cdot,\cdot)$ linear in its first argument. Use
$p\cdot a:=p^0a^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf a$ on $\mathbb R^4$, the convention
of the proper-orthochronous Poincaré supplier, and put
$$\overline V_+:=\{p=(p^0,\mathbf p)\in\mathbb R^4:p^0\ge|\mathbf p|\},\qquad V_+:=\{b=(b^0,\mathbf b)\in\mathbb R^4:b^0>|\mathbf b|\}.$$
For estimates only, write
$|p|_{\mathrm E}:=\sqrt{(p^0)^2+|\mathbf p|^2}$.

Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb R^4$:
each $E(S)$ is an orthogonal projection, $E(\varnothing)=0$,
$E(\mathbb R^4)=I$, $E(S\cap T)=E(S)E(T)$, and for every disjoint sequence
$(S_n)$, $E(\bigcup_nS_n)\xi=\sum_nE(S_n)\xi$ in norm for each
$\xi\in\mathcal H$. For a bounded Borel function $g$, write
$\Phi_E(g):=\int g(p)\,dE(p)$ for its bounded spectral integral, defined by
uniform simple-function approximation. Let
$U:\mathbb R^4\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary
representation of translations: $U(0)=I$, $U(a+a')=U(a)U(a')$, every $U(a)$
is a surjective linear isometry, and $a\mapsto U(a)\xi$ is norm-continuous for
each $\xi\in\mathcal H$. The **positive-energy joint spectral input** is the
additional data and condition
$$U(a)=\Phi_E\bigl(p\mapsto e^{ip\cdot a}\bigr),\qquad E(\mathbb R^4\setminus\overline V_+)=0.$$

Fix a translation-invariant unit vector $\Omega\in\mathcal H$, so $U(a)\Omega=\Omega$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^4$, and a specified unital $*$-subalgebra
$\mathfrak A\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$: it contains $I$ and is closed
under complex linear combinations, operator composition, and Hilbert-space
adjoints, with these operations inherited from $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Require
$\overline{\{A\Omega:A\in\mathfrak A\}}=\mathcal H$; this is the meaning of
cyclic vacuum here. If local bounded operators are used, their assignment
$O\mapsto\mathfrak A(O)\subseteq\mathfrak A$ for bounded open
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ is separately specified. This input asserts no
locality, isotony, covariance, or field-domain property for that assignment.
The PVM and its joint support are input; separate generators or a
matrix-coefficient Fourier-support condition do not replace this additional
data.

items.title: Positive spectrum gives bounded future-tube continuation

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019)
references.locator: §5.1, printed p. 24, Definition 24; §5.2, printed p. 25, proof of Theorem 26: positive spectrum gives a holomorphic translation extension and bounded insertions give holomorphic matrix coefficients.

references.title: Jens Mund, General Aspects of Relativistic Quantum Field Theory, incomplete lecture notes, DF-UFJF (2012)
references.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.8 and discussion, PDF pp. 18–19: Fourier support in the forward cone gives tube holomorphy and distributional boundary values. The notes refer the theorem's proof to other sources; the complete bounded-operator argument is supplied locally here.

references.title: Luis Álvarez-Gaumé and Miguel A. Vázquez-Mozo, General properties of noncommutative field theories, arXiv:hep-th/0305093 (2003)
references.locator: §4, PDF pp. 12–13: Wightman functions, tube continuation, and bounded-insertion CPT proof interface; cited only for the analytic route and its hypotheses, not as a standard scalar/spinor theorem.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the positive-energy joint spectral input of
[[def-qftx-joint-spectrum-input]] on $\mathcal H$. Put
$\mathcal T_+:=\{a+ib:a\in\mathbb R^4,\ b\in V_+\}$ and, for
$z=a+ib\in\mathcal T_+$, define
$$U(z):=\Phi_E\bigl(p\mapsto\mathbf1_{\overline V_+}(p)e^{ip\cdot z}\bigr), \qquad p\cdot z:=p^0z^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf z.$$
Then $U(z)$ is a bounded operator with $\|U(z)\|\le1$; the same formula
extends it to a strongly continuous contraction-valued map on
$\mathbb R^4+i\overline V_+$ and agrees with the given $U(a)$ when $b=0$.
Holomorphic means complex differentiable as a map of the full complex
coordinate vector, with a complex-linear total derivative and remainder
$o(\|h\|)$.

For every integer $n\ge1$, every $B_1,\ldots,B_{n-1}\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$,
and every $\psi,\phi\in\mathcal H$, the matrix coefficient
$$F(z_1,\ldots,z_n):= \bigl(U(z_1)B_1U(z_2)\cdots B_{n-1}U(z_n)\psi,\phi\bigr)$$
is holomorphic on $\mathcal T_+^n$, where each
$\operatorname{Im}z_j\in V_+$. No locality assumption on the bounded
insertions is used. This result concerns bounded operators; it asserts no
domain, product, or holomorphy claim for unbounded Wightman fields.

items.title: CPT and spin-statistics proof interface

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019)
references.locator: §5.2, printed p. 25, proof of Theorem 26: bounded-insertion tube functions and the explicit edge-of-the-wedge invocation; the theorem proved there is Reeh–Schlieder.

references.title: Jens Mund, General Aspects of Relativistic Quantum Field Theory, incomplete lecture notes, DF-UFJF (2012)
references.locator: §2.1, Theorems 2.6 and 2.8, PDF pp. 15–19: the exact reconstruction hypotheses, Fourier-support tube continuation, and an edge-of-the-wedge statement; the notes identify Theorem 2.8's proof as a reference rather than a local proof.

references.title: Luis Álvarez-Gaumé and Miguel A. Vázquez-Mozo, General properties of noncommutative field theories, arXiv:hep-th/0305093 (2003)
references.locator: §4, PDF pp. 12–19: the scalar noncommutative CPT proof interface, including tube/complex-group continuation and weak locality; §4.3 records limits on spin-statistics. Used as a scoped analytic comparison, not as a general scalar/spinor theorem.

items.statement:
A **CPT/spin-statistics proof interface** is the minimum set of typed data,
hypotheses, and proof obligations that must be fixed before a scalar or spinor
Wightman CPT or spin-statistics theorem is stated. It is a checklist, not a
sufficiency theorem, and it asserts neither conclusion.

The proposed field system must specify a nonzero complex Hilbert space
$\mathcal H$ as in “Hilbert space”, with inner product linear in its
first argument as in “Real and complex inner-product spaces and their induced length”, a dense
complex linear field domain
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}\subseteq\mathcal H$, and a finite-dimensional
complex component space $V$ with $1\le\dim_{\mathbb C}V<\infty$, together with a
distinguished unit vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$. A field multiplet is a finite family of complex-linear maps on Schwartz test functions, with the Schwartz topology of “Schwartz space and its seminorms” and the Poincaré pullback convention of “Proper-orthochronous Poincaré action and test pullback”:
$\Phi_\alpha:\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)\to
\operatorname{Lin}(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}})$, where
$\operatorname{Lin}(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}})$ is the vector space of
linear maps from that domain to itself. Each field map preserves
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$ and is weakly tempered: for every
$u,v\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$,
$f\mapsto(\Phi_\alpha(f)u,v)$ is a continuous linear functional on Schwartz
space. Every finite product on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$ must be defined.
For $g=(A,a)$, use $T_gf(x)=f(\Lambda(A)^{-1}(x-a))$.
The Poincaré pullback continuity lemma guarantees $T_gf\in\mathcal S$
and continuity of $T_g$ and $T_{g^{-1}}$ in the Schwartz topology, so
field covariance with these transformed tests is defined on the declared domain.
The associated
$n$-point function is the multilinear functional
$$(f_1,\ldots,f_n)\longmapsto (\Phi_{\alpha_1}(f_1)\cdots\Phi_{\alpha_n}(f_n)\Omega,\Omega);$$
the interface must require and identify its continuous extension to
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{4n};\mathbb C)$ for each component sequence.

The domain must satisfy $U(g)\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}=\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$ for every group element $g$. The symmetry
data must include a strongly continuous unitary group representation $U$ of
the spin-cover Poincaré group
$\widetilde P^\uparrow_+:=SL(2,\mathbb C)\ltimes\mathbb R^4$, with product
$(A,a)(B,b)=(AB,a+\Lambda(A)b)$. Give $SL(2,\mathbb C)$ its subspace topology
from $M_2(\mathbb C)$ and the semidirect product the product topology. Here
$SL(2,\mathbb C)=\{A\in M_2(\mathbb C):\det A=1\}$, and $GL(V)$ denotes the
invertible complex-linear maps on $V$. The specified continuous surjective
double-cover homomorphism
$\Lambda:SL(2,\mathbb C)\to SO^+(1,3)$ has kernel $\{I,-I\}$; $-I$ is the
central order-two kernel element called the $2\pi$-rotation element here.
$SO^+(1,3)$ and the affine translation conventions are those of the
Poincaré supplier. Each $U(g)$ is a surjective linear isometry of
$\mathcal H$, $U(gh)=U(g)U(h)$, and $g\mapsto U(g)\xi$ is norm-continuous
for each fixed $\xi\in\mathcal H$. The field system also specifies a
continuous finite-dimensional representation $S:SL(2,\mathbb C)\to GL(V)$,
so $S(AB)=S(A)S(B)$ and $S(I)=I$.
Its field covariance identity must be stated explicitly as an equality in
$\operatorname{Lin}(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}})$ and checked against the
group law. It must identify whether the component matrix is $S$, its dual, or
its complex conjugate and fix the test-function pullback or its inverse, the
adjoint convention, and all component indices. The vacuum $\Omega$ must be invariant under
translations, with translation-invariant subspace exactly $\mathbb C\Omega$,
and cyclic: the span of all vectors
$\Phi_{\alpha_1}(f_1)\cdots\Phi_{\alpha_n}(f_n)\Omega$, including $\Omega$,
is dense in $\mathcal H$.

The positive-energy premise must be the joint PVM input of
“Positive-energy joint spectral input”, including its Countable Choice assumption, on this same $\mathcal H$ with
this same $\Omega$. Denote its translation representation by
$U_{\mathrm{spec}}$ and require
$$U((I,a))=U_{\mathrm{spec}}(a)=\Phi_E(p\mapsto e^{ip\cdot a})\qquad(a\in\mathbb R^4).$$
For $f,g\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ with compact spacelike-separated
supports, the field locality identity and its sign must be stated on
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$. Here $\operatorname{supp}f$ is the closure of
$\{x:f(x)\ne0\}$. Spacelike separation here means
$(x^0-y^0)^2-|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2<0$ for every support pair. If a proof
uses **weak locality**, that term means the equality of the original and
reversed vacuum $n$-point distributions on the specific real set of relative
coordinates required by the selected theorem; the set, reversal, field
grading, and distributional boundary interpretation must be stated rather
than left under the name “Jost points.”

The proof interface must then identify, with the Fourier sign and relative
coordinates fixed, the multivariable tube domain to which each $n$-point
distribution is continued. A **complexified Lorentz action** here is a
specified holomorphic action on $\mathbb C^4$ of a specified complex matrix
group extending the real action through $\Lambda$ and preserving the
complex-bilinear extension of the Minkowski form. A **complex Lorentz
extension** means a single-valued holomorphic continuation on a stated domain
generated by that action; the acting group, its action, and the domain must be
given and the covariance formula checked there. Any
**edge-of-the-wedge** step must name its exact theorem, both holomorphic
domains, their common distributional boundary value, the open real set where
they agree, and the conclusion of uniqueness used.

A claimed **CPT conclusion** means the combined field transformation by
charge conjugation and spacetime inversion $x\mapsto-x$ (simultaneous parity
and time reversal); it must preserve
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$, define a surjective conjugate-linear isometry
$\Theta:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$ (antiunitarity), state its action on
$\Omega$, translations, every field component, and test functions, and specify
the conjugate-linear charge-conjugation map and all phases. A claimed
**spin-statistics
conclusion** must state the action $S(-I)=\epsilon_{\rm spin}I_V$ of the
central $2\pi$-rotation element $-I\in SL(2,\mathbb C)$, with
$\epsilon_{\rm spin}\in\{+1,-1\}$, and the actual spacelike exchange sign
$\epsilon_{\rm loc}\in\{+1,-1\}$ in
$\Phi_\alpha(f)\Phi_\beta(g)=\epsilon_{\rm loc}\Phi_\beta(g)\Phi_\alpha(f)$
on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{field}}$. For a multiplet with a single spin parity, the theorem must
derive the precise relation $\epsilon_{\mathrm{loc}}=\epsilon_{\mathrm{spin}}$. Any additional
theorem-specific assumptions remain explicit; this interface does not claim
that its checklist alone suffices.

title: Positive-energy tube analyticity and discrete-symmetry proof interfaces — Examples

items.title: One positive frequency decays in the future imaginary direction

references.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, arXiv:1904.04051v2 (2019)
references.locator: §§5.1–5.2, printed pp. 24–25: the translation Fourier sign, positive spectrum, future-tube extension, and bounded-insertion example in the Reeh–Schlieder proof.

references.title: Jens Mund, General Aspects of Relativistic Quantum Field Theory, incomplete lecture notes, DF-UFJF (2012)
references.locator: §1.3, PDF pp. 8–9, equation (22), and §2.1, Theorem 2.8, PDF pp. 18–19: the positive-energy Fourier convention and the sign of the distributional tube.

items.statement:
Let $p\in\overline V_+$ be nonzero, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with
standard basis $e_0,e_1$, and set $\Omega=e_0$,
$E_p(S)=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf1_S(0),\mathbf1_S(p))$, and
$U_p(a)=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{ip\cdot a})$. Take
$\mathfrak A=\mathcal B(\mathbb C^2)$. These data give a positive-energy joint
spectral input with a translation-invariant cyclic vacuum: the zero mode fixes
$\Omega$, while $e_1$ carries one nonzero positive frequency. The continuation
is $U_p(a+ib)=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{ip\cdot a-p\cdot b})$. For every
$b\in V_+$, the $e_1$ component decays by $e^{-p\cdot b}<1$; the vacuum
component remains $1$, so the full operator norm is exactly $1$. Reversing the
Fourier sign gives $U_p^-(a+ib)=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{-ip\cdot a+p\cdot b})$,
which grows on $e_1$ in the future imaginary direction and decays there in the
past direction. This finite-spectrum example illustrates the Fourier-sign
convention; it is not a claim about a physical field or a general Wightman
theorem.
